approachQuestion.prompt:
Unrepeated Access Records

An array `records` contains integer visitor identifiers in chronological order. Return the length of the longest contiguous segment in which no identifier appears more than once. Identifiers may recur anywhere in the array. Return 0 for an empty array.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; -10^9 ≤ records[i] ≤ 10^9.
• Leave the input unchanged. Identifiers and indices fit in a machine word.

Examples:
1. records = [9,4,7,4,8] → 3, for [9,4,7] or [7,4,8].
2. records = [2,5,5,2] → 2.
3. records = [] → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: Leave the input unchanged. Identifiers and indices fit in a machine word.

options.text: Keep a hash table from identifier to latest index. At index right, if the identifier has appeared, set left to max(left, latest + 1). Update its latest index and the best length.
options.feedback: The max prevents a repeat outside the current segment from moving left backward. The segment after the jump has no duplicate.

options.text: Binary-search the greatest feasible length. For each trial scan every segment of that length with a frequency table to check whether some segment has all distinct identifiers.
options.feedback: Feasibility is monotone: a distinct segment contains distinct shorter segments. Repeated full feasibility passes can be avoided by maintaining the left boundary directly.

options.text: Keep latest indices, but on every repeated identifier set left to latest + 1 even when that is smaller than the current left. Then update the best length.
options.feedback: On [2,5,5,2], left becomes 2 at the second 5, then incorrectly moves back to 1 at the final 2, accepting [5,5,2] of length three.

options.text: Return the number of different identifiers in the whole array.
options.feedback: For [1,2,1,3,1,4], there are four different identifiers but no distinct contiguous segment longer than three.

feedback.reason: Set left=max(left,previous+1), never simply previous+1: an old occurrence outside the current window must not move left backward.
details: Start left and best at zero. For each right index, read the previous index for its identifier from a hash table if present, set left to the greater of left and previous + 1, store right as the latest index, and update best from right - left + 1. Retain table entries even when they lie before left.

Set left=max(left,previous+1), never simply previous+1: an old occurrence outside the current window must not move left backward. Retained latest-position entries may outlive the current window and still count as auxiliary storage.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Jump past the last occurrence” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair under the stated expected hashing model.
constraints: Use expected constant-time hash lookup and insertion with amortized resizing; include all table storage and resizing work. Collisions are handled correctly.
Analyze the stated table method, retaining all latest indices; do not substitute a different algorithm.
Input and the scalar output are excluded. No segment is copied. Arithmetic and random access are unit cost; the iterative call stack is constant.

options.text: Expected O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
Expected O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
Expected O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Expected constant map work per position retains all observed identifier entries.
details: There are a constant number of hash-table operations per input position, so expected total time is O(n). The table retains up to n different identifiers, giving O(n) auxiliary space in the worst case. The left boundary never retreats, and the previous occurrence of the incoming identifier is the only newly introduced conflict.
“Expected O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Latest-index jumps avoid restarting from each left boundary. There are only constant-many expected map operations per right index.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The stated hash model gives expected constant operations; no balanced tree or sorting introduces a log n factor.
“Expected O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The map retains the latest index of every observed identifier, including entries before left; distinct input needs n entries.
